{{nihongo|'''Katsuhiko Sato'''|佐藤 勝彦|Satō Katsuhiko|extra=August 30, 1945}} is a Japanese physicist and Special University Professor, emeritus, the [[University of Tokyo]].

Professor Sato published a paper advocating [[cosmic inflation]] in 1981, but it was not widely recognized by Western academic circles.

== Life ==
Katsuhiko Sato was born in [[Sakaide]], [[Kagawa Prefecture]], Japan on August 30, 1945. He graduated from the Department of Physics, Faculty of Science, [[Kyoto University]], and received a Doctor of Science degree. 

Since he was a graduate student, Sato has been conducting research on [[supernovae]], following the advice of his mentor, [[Chushiro Hayashi]]. Among other things he conducted research on the influence of [[neutrinos]] in supernovae.

Sato has served as a research assistant at Kyoto University, a visiting professor at the [[Nordic Institute for Theoretical Physics]], an associate professor/professor at the [[University of Tokyo]], the Chairman of 47th Committee of the [[International Astronomical Union]], and the president of the [[Physical Society of Japan]].

== Origin of the Inflation  ==
Sato proposed [[Inflation (cosmology)|inflationary cosmology]] in 1981, around the same time as [[Alan Guth]]. Sato was the first to submit a paper on this theory,<ref name="k. sato">{{Cite journal
|first = K.
|last = Sato
|bibcode = 1981MNRAS.195..467S
|title = First-order phase transition of a vacuum and the expansion of the Universe
|journal = Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
|volume = 195
|issue = 3
|page = 467
|year = 1981
|doi = 10.1093/mnras/195.3.467
|doi-access = free
}}</ref><ref name="guth">{{Cite journal
|first = A. H.
|last = Guth
|title = The Inflatsonary Universe: A Possible Solution to the Horizon and Flatness Problems
|journal = Phys. Rev. D
|volume = 23
|issue = 2
|page = 347
|year = 1981
|bibcode=1981PhRvD..23..347G
|doi = 10.1103/PhysRevD.23.347
}}</ref> Guth presented an inflation model similar to Sato's at a seminar at [[Stanford University]] in January 1980.<ref name="SLAC">{{Citation
|publisher = [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]] seminar
|contribution = 10-35 seconds after the Big Bang
|date = 23 January 1980
}} see Guth (1997), p. 186</ref> [[Alexei Starobinsky]] also presented the idea of a similar model in 1979 <ref>{{Cite journal
|last = Starobinsky
|first = A. A.
|title = Spectrum Of Relict Gravitational Radiation And The Early State Of The Universe
|journal = JETP Letters
|volume = 30
|page = 682
|year = 1979
|bibcode = 1979JETPL..30..682S
}}; {{Cite journal
|journal = Pisma Zh. Eksp. Teor. Fiz.
|volume = 30
|page = 719
|year = 1979
}}</ref> and published a paper in 1980.<ref name="starobinsky">{{Cite journal
|first = Alexei A.
|last = Starobinsky
|title = A new type of isotropic cosmological models without singularity
|journal = Phys. Lett.
|volume = B91
|pages = 99&ndash;102
|year = 1980
|issue = 1
|doi = 10.1016/0370-2693(80)90670-X
|bibcode = 1980PhLB...91...99S
}}</ref>

Alan Guth was the first to use the term "inflation". Sato originally used the term "exponential expansion model". Sato said:
<blockquote>
"I originally called this model the 'exponential expansion model.' However, American astrophysicist Guth published a similar model six months later, cleverly naming it the 'Inflation  model.' That's why it It's like this." It's now called inflation theory."<ref name="inflation_naming">佐藤勝彦著『相対性理論から100年でわかったこと』（PHP研究所 (2010/9/18) ISBN 978-4569774824）203ページ</ref>
</blockquote>

[[JAXA]] Space Information Center describes it as follows:
<blockquote>
Katsuhiko Sato published his theory of inflation in 1981. Alan Harvey Goose also published his theory of inflation around the same time as Sato, but Sato published his paper earlier.<ref name="jaxa">{{Cite web
|publisher = JAXA, 宇宙情報センター
|title = 佐藤勝彦
|url = http://spaceinfo.jaxa.jp/ja/sato_katsuhiko.html
|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110603094554/http://spaceinfo.jaxa.jp/ja/sato_katsuhiko.html
|accessdate= 2015-10-20
|archive-date = 2011-06-03
}}</ref>
</blockquote>

== Academic genealogy ==
Sato studied under the world-renowned astronomer [[Chushiro Hayashi]], who was a student of [[Hideki Yukawa]], Japan's first Nobel Prize winner. 

On October 8, 2002, Sato was the first person to receive a call from the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] to the Koshiba Laboratory informing [[Masatoshi Koshiba]] that he had won this year's [[Nobel Prize in Physics]]. Sato and [[Yoji Totsuka]] decided to attend Koshiba's press conference that evening together. Sato sat to the left of Koshiba at the press conference.<ref>[https://www.rochester.edu/newscenter/nobel-prize-laureate-remembered-for-groundbreaking-research-on-neutrinos-461492/ Nobel Prize laureate remembered for groundbreaking research on neutrinos]</ref> In any case, Japan's leading group of astronomers maintained close contacts.

== Recognition ==
*1989 - Inoue Prize for Science
*1990 - [[Nishina Memorial Prize]]
*2002 - [[Medals of Honor (Japan)|Medal with Purple Ribbon]]
*2010 - [[Japan Academy Prize (academics)|Japan Academy Prize]]
*2014 - [[Person of Cultural Merit]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.asahi.com/articles/ASGBQ46FTGBQUCVL001.html |title=存档副本 |access-date=2015-03-28 |archive-date=2015-07-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150715013741/http://www.asahi.com/articles/ASGBQ46FTGBQUCVL001.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*2018 - [[Order of the Sacred Treasure]]

== Namesakes and popular culture ==
The asteroid [[7965 Katsuhiko]], discovered in 1996, was named after Professor Sato.

In the Japanese role-playing video game ''[[Shin Megami Tensei If...]]'', a character "Sato" is named after Professor Sato.
